studies.label: Laboratory experiment: AI instruction, human instruction, or rest; AUT acquisition and transfer

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract (total randomized); PDF p. 3, Section 2.1 Participants (randomized arm counts); two verbatim excerpts
counts_source.quote:
95 participants were randomized into AI instruction, human instruction, or control conditions.
AI (n = 31, 27 females), human (n = 34, 21 females), and control (n = 30, 28 females).

arms.name: AI instruction
arms.description: Real-time, participant-directed text dialogue with ChatGPT-4.0 as a creativity instructor, using a common guideline, example prompts and backup learning materials; instruction lasted approximately 8 to 10 minutes. Researchers monitored the chats for adherence to the instructional protocol (PDF p. 4, Section 2.3).

arms.name: Human instruction
arms.description: Individual face-to-face heuristic instruction from trained postgraduate education students, following standardized scripts on association, decomposition and combination, for the same duration as AI instruction (PDF p. 4, Section 2.3).

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Quiet rest with eyes closed for the same duration, without instruction or interaction (PDF p. 4, Section 2.3).

studies.country: China (inferred from the institutional setting; recruitment country is not explicitly stated)
studies.task: Participants listed creative uses for books before instruction and then for books again (acquisition), umbrellas and can (transfer), with three minutes per AUT item (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4.0
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 2.3: 'Under the AI instruction condition, participants interacted directly with ChatGPT-4.0 in real time.' No release year or model snapshot is specified.

estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two trained independent raters rated each idea on a five-point originality scale, from not at all original to very original, after pooling responses and removing duplicates. Rater scores were averaged to yield a participant score. Aggregation across a participant's ideas is not specified (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2).

sources.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1 Creativity performance, Learning outcome

sources.quote: Their ratings were then averaged to yield each participant's fluency, originality, and flexibility scores.

sources.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1 Creativity performance, Learning outcome, post hoc comparisons
sources.quote: Moreover, the post-test originality and flexibility scores also significantly higher than the posttest scores of human instructor group and control group, ps ≤0.04.

estimates.notes: Post-test comparison after the instruction phase, in the same session; AI availability during the post-test is inferred to be absent from the separate instruction and post-test phases (PDF pp. 4-5, Section 2.4). The comparator's mean and SD appear only as bars and error bars in Figure 2 (PDF p. 6), so they are null. The dispersion following ± in the prose is recorded as SD, consistent with the accompanying figure caption ('Error bars indicate standard deviations.'). Analyzed counts are not explicitly printed for this contrast; assignment counts and degrees of freedom are not substituted. The reported omnibus time-by-instruction and instruction main-effect tests do not estimate this pairwise contrast; their F statistics and partial eta-squared values are not entered in stats. The study assigns instruction between participants; repeated pre/post measurement does not make this a randomized-order within-person comparison. The p_value is the bound reported jointly for the relevant post hoc comparisons in the prose, not an exact pairwise p-value. Values available only in the figure are not transcribed, following extraction rule 1. The repeated 'books' item was also an explicit example in the AI instructional prompts; acquisition could include recall of ideas from instruction (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 2.2-2.3).

not_extracted.what: Omnibus AUT time, instruction type and time-by-instruction ANOVA tests
not_extracted.reason: These full-design tests do not identify a contrast between two named arms; their F statistics and partial eta-squared values cannot be substituted for the requested pairwise effects (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.1).

open_items: The separate supplement is not saved locally and was not retrieved. PDF p. 5, Section 3 cites Table S2 for descriptive means and SDs but does not establish whether it contains post-test descriptives. PDF p. 12, Appendix A points to the article DOI. Human and control post-test means and SDs remain unavailable outside the figure.

PDF p. 5 labels AI acquisition flexibility as 7.29 ± 2.97, but the pre/post bar heights in PDF p. 6, Figure 2C appear inconsistent with that post-test value. Retain the printed prose value pending Table S2 or an author correction.

The paper explicitly prints randomized counts but not analyzed counts for the study, arms or individual creativity contrasts. No analyzed counts are derived from degrees of freedom or by adding assignment counts.
PDF p. 3, Section 2.2 does not specify how originality ratings across a participant's ideas are aggregated; averaging the two raters does not answer this.
The aggregation of the 'umbrellas' and 'can' post-test item scores into the transfer outcome is not stated (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2; PDF p. 6, Section 3.1).
The separate instruction and post-test phases support after_ai, but the paper does not explicitly state that ChatGPT was unavailable during the post-test (PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 2.3-2.4).

No pairwise difference, SE, confidence interval, test statistic or standardized effect is printed in the prose for the extracted contrasts. Prose p-values are joint bounds for selected pairwise comparisons; more specific values that appear only in the figure are not transcribed under extraction rule 1.
The paper names ChatGPT-4.0 but supplies neither a model release year nor a dated model snapshot; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF p. 4, Section 2.3).

Student status is supported by university-advertisement recruitment and the 'Student' labels in Figure 1A, but enrollment of all participants and the recruitment country are not explicitly stated (PDF pp. 3-4).
notes: Extracted independently by A on 2026-10-10. The complete saved markdown was read from beginning through Appendix A and the references. Cited PDF pages were checked with pymupdf text extraction; Figures 1 and 2 were inspected in memory without creating image files. The reconciled form was used as a map, not as the source of the numbers. All six AUT outcomes and both AI-versus-comparator records per outcome are retained, including incomplete records with only the printed AI-arm level. Numerical values available only from figures were not transcribed. All recorded means, SDs and p-value bounds are in the prose. Printed decimal precision is retained in the verbatim source quotes. Participant-level sd_level follows the scoring method; se_basis is participant where a post hoc pairwise test is reported, including the figure-only transfer-originality comparison against Control, and not_reported where no pairwise uncertainty is reported. Randomized arm sizes are kept only in the study record. Analyzed counts are null even though the screening form inferred them from degrees of freedom. The counts_source combines two identified verbatim excerpts: the abstract total and the Methods arm counts. The paper names no preregistration or primary outcome. No shared sample with another paper is stated. AI role is open_chat because participants could initiate and follow up on questions and request original ideas; the interaction was not restricted to content-free coaching. Country is inferred from the Shanghai Normal University setting and ethics approval; population follows university recruitment and the student labels in Figure 1A. The supplement manifest contains no local supplement file. Direct urllib requests to the named ScienceDirect article and Crossref API, using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, both failed with WinError 10013 in this environment. PDF p. 12 says the data are available from the corresponding authors for research purposes only. No author was contacted, and no data or other file was downloaded. No standardized effect, difference, analysis count, or uncertainty was computed.
